entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 11 Is 11:1-16 . From the local and temporary national deliverance the prophet passes by the law of suggestion in an easy transition to the end of all prophecy-- the everlasting deliverance under Messiah's reign, not merely His first coming, but chiefly His second coming. The language and illustrations are still drawn from the temporary national subject, with which he began, but the glories described pertain to Messiah's reign. Hezekiah cannot, as some think, be the subject; for he was already come, whereas the "stem of Jesse" was yet future ("shall come") (compare Mi 4:11 , &c.; 5:1, 2; Jr 23:5 , 6 ; 33:15 , 16 ; Ro 15:12 ). 1. rod-- When the proud "boughs" of "Lebanon" ( Is 10:33 , 34 , the Assyrians) are lopped, and the vast "forests cut down" amidst all this rage, a seemingly humble rod shall come out of Jesse (Messiah), who shall retrieve the injuries done by the Assyrian "rod" to Israel ( Is 10:5 , 6, 18, 19). stem-- literally, "the stump" of a tree cut close by the roots: happily expressing the depressed state of the royal house of David, owing to the hostile storm ( Is 10:18 , 19 ), when Messiah should arise from it, to raise it to more than its pristine glory. Lu 2:7 proves this ( Is 53:2 ; compare Job 14:7 , 8 ; see on Is 8:6 ). Branch-- Scion. He is nevertheless also the "root" ( Is 11:10 ; Re 5:5 ; 22:16 . "Root and offspring" combines both, Zec 3:8 ; 6:12 ).

Spirit of the Lord--</hi>Jehovah. The Spirit by which the prophets spake: for Messiah was to be a Prophet (<reference osisRef="Isa.61.1">Is 61:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Deut.18.15">De 18:15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Deut.18.18">18</reference>). Seven gifts of the Holy Spirit are specified, to imply that the perfection of them was to be in Him. Compare "the seven Spirits" (<reference osisRef="Rev.1.4">Re 1:4</reference>), that is, the Holy Ghost in His perfect fulness: seven being the sacred number. The prophets had only a portion out of the "fulness" in the Son of God (<reference osisRef="John.1.16">Joh 1:16</reference>; 3:34; <reference osisRef="Col.1.19">Col 1:19</reference>).<div eID="gen13887" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13888" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">rest--</hi>permanently; not merely come upon Him (<reference osisRef="Num.11.25">Nu 11:25</reference>, <reference osisRef="Num.11.26">26</reference>).<div eID="gen13888" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13889" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">wisdom--</hi>(<reference osisRef="1Cor.1.30">1Co 1:30</reference>; <reference osisRef="Eph.1.17">Ep 1:17</reference>; <reference osisRef="Col.2.3">Col 2:3</reference>).<div eID="gen13889" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13890" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">understanding--</hi>coupled with "wisdom," being its fruit. Discernment and discrimination (<reference osisRef="Matt.22.18">Mt 22:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.2.25">Joh 2:25</reference>).<div eID="gen13890" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13891" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">counsel ... might--</hi>the faculty of forming counsels, and that of executing them (<reference osisRef="Isa.28.29">Is 28:29</reference>). Counsellor (<reference osisRef="Isa.9.6">Is 9:6</reference>).<div eID="gen13891" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13892" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">knowledge--</hi>of the deep things of God (<reference osisRef="Matt.11.27">Mt 11:27</reference>). The knowledge of Him gives us true knowledge (<reference osisRef="Eph.1.17">Ep 1:17</reference>).<div eID="gen13892" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13893" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">fear of the Lord--</hi>reverential, obedient fear. The first step towards true "knowledge" (<reference osisRef="Job.28.28">Job 28:28</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.111.10">Psa 111:10</reference>). <div eID="gen13893" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8529"/><div sID="gen13894" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8529"/><hi type="bold">3. make him of quick understanding--</hi>literally, "quick-scented in the fear of Jehovah"; endowed with a singular sagacity in discerning the genuine principle of religious fear of God, when it lies dormant in the yet unawakened sinner (<reference osisRef="Matt.12.20">Mt 12:20</reference>; Ac 10:1-48; 16:14) [Horsley]. But Maurer, "He shall delight in the fear of God." The Hebrew means "to delight in the odors" of anything (<reference osisRef="Exod.30.38">Ex 30:38</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.5.21">Am 5:21</reference>); "smell," that is, "delight in."<div eID="gen13894" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13895" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">after ... sight--</hi>according to mere external appearances (<reference osisRef="John.7.24">Joh 7:24</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.8.15">8:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jas.2.1">Jas 2:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Sam.16.7">1Sa 16:7</reference>). Herein Messiah is represented a just Judge and Ruler (<reference osisRef="Deut.1.16">De 1:16</reference>, <reference osisRef="1Cor.1.17">17</reference>).<div eID="gen13895" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13896" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">reprove--</hi>"decide," as the parallelism shows.<div eID="gen13896" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13897" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">after ... ears--</hi>by mere plausible hearsays, but by the true merits of each case (<reference osisRef="John.6.64">Joh 6:64</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.2.23">Re 2:23</reference>). <div eID="gen13897" type="x-p"/>

"Judge" may mean here "rule," as in <reference osisRef="Ps.67.4">Psa 67:4</reference>.<div eID="gen13898" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13899" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">reprove--</hi>or, "argue"; "decide." But Lowth, "work conviction in."<div eID="gen13899" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13900" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">earth--</hi>Compare with <reference osisRef="Matt.5.5">Mt 5:5</reference>, and <reference osisRef="Rev.11.15">Re 11:15</reference>.<div eID="gen13900" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13901" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">earth--</hi>its ungodly inhabitants, answering to "the wicked" in the parallel, and in antithesis to the "poor" and "meek," namely, in spirit, the humble pious (<reference osisRef="Matt.5.3">Mt 5:3</reference>). It is at the same time implied that "the earth" will be extraordinarily wicked when He shall come to judge and reign. His reign shall therefore be ushered in with judgments on the apostates (<reference osisRef="Ps.2.9-Ps.2.12">Psa 2:9-12</reference>; <reference osisRef="Luke.18.8">Lu 18:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.2.27">Re 2:27</reference>).<div eID="gen13901" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13902" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">rod of ... mouth--</hi>condemning sentences which proceed from His mouth against the wicked (<reference osisRef="Rev.1.16">Re 1:16</reference>; 2:16; 19:15, 21).<div eID="gen13902" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13903" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">breath of ... lips--</hi>his judicial decisions (<reference osisRef="Isa.30.28">Is 30:28</reference>; <reference osisRef="Job.15.30">Job 15:30</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.19.20">Re 19:20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.20.9-Rev.20.12">20:9-12</reference>). He as the Word of God (<reference osisRef="Rev.19.13-Rev.19.15">Re 19:13-15</reference>) comes to strike that blow which shall decide His claim to the kingdom, previously usurped by Satan, and "the beast" to whom Satan delegates his power. It will be a day of judgment to the Gentile dispensation, as the first coming was to the Jews. Compare a type of the "rod" (<reference osisRef="Num.17.2-Num.17.10">Nu 17:2-10</reference>). <div eID="gen13903" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8532"/><div sID="gen13905" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8532"/><hi type="bold">6. wolf ... lamb--</hi>Each animal is coupled with that one which is its natural prey. A fit state of things under the "Prince of Peace" (<reference osisRef="Isa.65.25">Is 65:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.34.25">Eze 34:25</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.2.18">Ho 2:18</reference>). These may be figures for men of corresponding animal-like characters (<reference osisRef="Ezek.22.27">Eze 22:27</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.38.13">38:13</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.5.6">Jr 5:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.13.23">13:23</reference>; <reference osisRef="Matt.7.15">Mt 7:15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Luke.10.3">Lu 10:3</reference>). Still a literal change in the relations of animals to man and each other, restoring the state in Eden, is a more likely interpretation. Compare <reference osisRef="Gen.2.19">Ge 2:19</reference>, 20, with <reference osisRef="Ps.8.6-Ps.8.8">Psa 8:6-8</reference>, which describes the restoration to man, in the person of "the Son of man," of the lost dominion over the animal kingdom of which he had been designed to be the merciful vicegerent under God, for the good of his animal subjects (<reference osisRef="Rom.8.19-Rom.8.22">Ro 8:19-22</reference>). <div eID="gen13905" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8536"/><div sID="gen13912" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8536"/><hi type="bold">10. root--</hi>rather, "shoot from the root" (compare Note, see on <reference osisRef="Isa.11.1">Is 11:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.53.2">Is 53:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.5.5">Re 5:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.22.16">22:16</reference>).<div eID="gen13912" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13913" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">stand--</hi>permanently and prominently, as a banner lifted up to be the rallying point of an army or people (<reference osisRef="Isa.5.26">Is 5:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="John.12.32">Joh 12:32</reference>).<div eID="gen13913" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13914" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">the people--</hi>peoples, answering to "the Gentiles" in the parallel member.<div eID="gen13914" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13915" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">to it ... seek--</hi>diligently (<reference osisRef="Job.8.5">Job 8:5</reference>). entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8537"/><div sID="gen13917" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8537"/><hi type="bold">11. set ... hand--</hi>take in hand the work. Therefore the coming restoration of the Jews is to be distinct from that after the Babylonish captivity, and yet to resemble it. The first restoration was literal, therefore so shall the second be; the latter, however, it is implied here, shall be much more universal than the former (Is 43:5-7; 49:12, 17, 18; <reference osisRef="Ezek.37.21">Eze 37:21</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hos.3.5">Ho 3:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.9.14">Am 9:14</reference>, <reference osisRef="Amos.9.15">15</reference>; <reference osisRef="Mic.4.6">Mi 4:6</reference>, <reference osisRef="Mic.4.7">7</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.19">Zep 3:19</reference>, <reference osisRef="Zeph.3.20">20</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.10.10">Zec 10:10</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.23.8">Jr 23:8</reference>). As to the "remnant" destined by God to survive the judgments on the nation, compare <reference osisRef="Jer.46.28">Jr 46:28</reference>.<div eID="gen13917" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13918" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Pathros--</hi>one of the three divisions of Egypt, Upper Egypt.<div eID="gen13918" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13919" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Cush--</hi>either Ethiopia, south of Egypt, now Abyssinia, or the southern parts of Arabia, along the Red Sea.<div eID="gen13919" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13920" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Elam--</hi>Persia, especially the southern part of it now called Susiana.<div eID="gen13920" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13921" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">Shinar--</hi>Babylonian Mesopotamia, the plain between the Euphrates and the Tigris: in it Babel was begun (<reference osisRef="Gen.10.10">Ge 10:10</reference>). In the Assyrian inscriptions Rawlinson distinguishes three periods: (1) The Chaldean; from 2300 B.C. to 1500, in which falls Chedorlaomer (<reference osisRef="Gen.14.1-Gen.14.17">Ge 14:1-17</reference>), called in the cuneiform characters Kudur of Hur, or Ur of the Chaldees, and described as the conqueror of Syria. The seat of the first Chaldean empire was in the south, towards the confluence of the Tigris and Euphrates. (2) The Assyrian, down to 625 B.C. (3) The Babylonian, from 625 to 538 B.C., when Babylon was taken by the Persian Cyrus.<div eID="gen13921" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13922" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">islands of ... sea--</hi>the far western regions beyond the sea [Jerome]. <div eID="gen13922" type="x-p"/>

The seat of the first Chaldean empire was in the south, towards the confluence of the Tigris and Euphrates. (2) The Assyrian, down to 625 B.C. (3) The Babylonian, from 625 to 538 B.C., when Babylon was taken by the Persian Cyrus. islands of ... sea-- the far western regions beyond the sea [Jerome].

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8538"/><div sID="gen13923" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8538"/>12. In the first restoration Judah alone was restored, with perhaps some few of Israel (the ten tribes): in the future restoration both are expressly specified (<reference osisRef="Ezek.37.16-Ezek.37.19">Eze 37:16-19</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.3.18">Jr 3:18</reference>). To Israel are ascribed the "outcasts" (masculine); to Judah the "dispersed" (feminine), as the former have been longer and more utterly castaways (though not finally) than the latter (<reference osisRef="John.7.52">Joh 7:52</reference>). The masculine and feminine conjoined express the universality of the restoration.<div eID="gen13923" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13924" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">from the four corners of the earth--</hi>Hebrew, "wings of the earth." <div eID="gen13924" type="x-p"/>

Judah--</hi>which began as early as the time (<reference osisRef="Judg.8.1">Jud 8:1</reference>; <reference osisRef="Judg.12.1">12:1</reference>, &c.). Joshua had sprung from, and resided among the Ephraimites (<reference osisRef="Num.13.9">Nu 13:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Josh.19.50">Jos 19:50</reference>); the sanctuary was with them for a time (<reference osisRef="Josh.18.1">Jos 18:1</reference>). The jealousy increased subsequently (<reference osisRef="2Sam.2.8">2Sa 2:8</reference>, &c.; 19:41; 20:<reference osisRef="2Cor.3.10">2; 3:10</reference>); and even before David's time (<reference osisRef="1Sam.11.8">1Sa 11:8</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Sam.15.4">15:4</reference>), they had appropriated to themselves the national name Israel. It ended in disruption (<reference osisRef="1Kgs.11.26">1Ki 11:26</reference>, &c.; <reference osisRef="1Kgs.12.1-1Kgs.12.33">1Ki 12:1-33</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="2Kgs.14.9">2Ki 14:9</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.78.56-Ps.78.71">Psa 78:56-71</reference>).<div eID="gen13925" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13926" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">adversaries of Judah--</hi>rather, "the adversaries from Judah"; those of Judah hostile to the Ephraimites [Maurer]. The parallelism "the envy of Ephraim," namely, against Judah, requires this, as also what follows; namely, "Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not vex Ephraim" (<reference osisRef="Ezek.37.15">Eze 37:15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.17.19">17, 19</reference>). <div eID="gen13926" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8541"/><div sID="gen13934" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8541"/>15. So the prophecies elsewhere (<reference osisRef="Ps.68.22">Psa 68:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="Exod.14.22">Ex 14:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="Zech.10.11">Zec 10:11</reference>). The same deliverance furnishes the imagery by which the return from Babylon is described (<reference osisRef="Isa.48.20">Is 48:20</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.48.21">21</reference>).<div eID="gen13934" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13935" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">destroy--</hi>literally, "devote," or "doom," that is, dry up; for what God dooms, perishes (<reference osisRef="Ps.106.9">Psa 106:9</reference> <reference osisRef="Nah.1.4">Na 1:4</reference>).<div eID="gen13935" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13936" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">tongue--</hi>the Bubastic branch of the Nile [Vitringa]; but as the Nile was not the obstruction to the exodus, it is rather the west tongue or Heroöpolite fork of the Red Sea.<div eID="gen13936" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13937" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">with ... mighty wind--</hi>such as the "strong east wind" (<reference osisRef="Exod.14.21">Ex 14:21</reference>), by which God made a way for Israel through the Red Sea. The Hebrew for "mighty" means terrible. Maurer translates, "With the terror of His anger"; that is, His terrible anger.<div eID="gen13937" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13938" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in the seven streams--</hi>rather, "shall smite it (divide it by smiting) into seven (many) streams, so as to be easily crossed" [Lowth]. So Cyrus divided the river Gyndes, which retarded his march against Babylon, into three hundred sixty streams, so that even a woman could cross it [Herodotus, 1.189]. "The river" is the Euphrates, the obstruction to Israel's return "from Assyria" (<reference osisRef="Isa.11.16">Is 11:16</reference>), a type of all future impediments to the restoration of the Jews.<div eID="gen13938" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen13939" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">dry shod--</hi>Hebrew, "in shoes." Maurer translates, "With the terror of His anger"; that is, His terrible anger. in the seven streams-- rather, "shall smite it (divide it by smiting) into seven (many) streams, so as to be easily crossed" [Lowth]. So Cyrus divided the river Gyndes, which retarded his march against Babylon, into three hundred sixty streams, so that even a woman could cross it [Herodotus, 1.189]. "The river" is the Euphrates, the obstruction to Israel's return "from Assyria" ( Is 11:16 ), a type of all future impediments to the restoration of the Jews. dry shod-- Hebrew, "in shoes." Even in sandals they should be able to pass over the once mighty river without being wet ( Re 16:12 ).

navigation_sections.title: CHAPTER 11
navigation_sections.content_plain: CHAPTER 11 Is 11:1-16 . From the local and temporary national deliverance the prophet passes by the law of suggestion in an easy transition to the end of all prophecy-- the everlasting deliverance under Messiah's reign, not merely His first coming, but chiefly His second coming. The language and illustrations are still drawn from the temporary national subject, with which he began, but the glories described pertain to Messiah's reign. Hezekiah cannot, as some think, be the subject; for he was already come, whereas the "stem of Jesse" was yet future ("shall come") (compare Mi 4:11 , &c.; 5:1, 2; Jr 23:5 , 6 ; 33:15 , 16 ; Ro 15:12 ).
